why: This week is Simulation, and the simulation here is a scan: for every non-zero cell, walk the square of radius matrix[i][j] around it (clipped to the board, corners skipped) and check that nothing in it is greater or equal. No clever structure is needed, because the stated limit allows O(rows^2 * cols^2).
hints: The region depends on the cell's own value v: rows i-v..i+v and columns j-v..j+v, clipped to the matrix.
A cell is a corner of its region exactly when |r-i| == v and |c-j| == v. Skip those four cells and the centre itself; any other cell with value >= v disqualifies it.
Loop over cells in row-major order, scan each region and stop at the first blocker. Appending in that order gives the required sorting for free. Worst case O(R^2 * C^2).
pitfalls: Zero cells are never local maximums, even when every neighbour is zero.
'Greater or equal' disqualifies, so two equal peaks that see each other both fail.
Only the four extreme corners are excluded, not whole corner regions. For v = 1 that leaves the 4 orthogonal neighbours.
constraints:
• Not stated in the source. Assume 1 ≤ rows, cols ≤ 100 and 0 ≤ matrix[i][j] ≤ 100.
  • The source allows time complexity up to O(rows² × cols²).
